chapter: New York and the swing years
title: Cab Calloway, California, and the Les Hite band
summary: Calloway's was his first big band; Milton Hinton replaced him. He stayed in California around 1934, then returned east in 1940 with Les Hite.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I'm trying to think, did you belong to any big band during the 30s? Yes, Cab Calloway.
That's what I was trying to think of. Yeah, Cab Calloway. That was my first big band.
Who's the other bass player? Is Rhythm in New York now? Oh, Hinton. Milton Hinton, yeah.
I was confused. I knew he was Rhythm. I couldn't remember.

Hinton, uh, no, yeah. After I left, Hinton took my place, because I was right here in California. See, I stayed out in California around 34. I didn't go back with Cab. I come out here with Cab a long time before. Then, then I went back east in 40, a little before the war, see. Yeah. And I went back with Les Hyde Band from here, from the west coast, the great Les Hyde. We went to the, uh, the Golden Gate. That's when the Golden Gate was in New York, a big place. Yeah, remember that. I stayed with Les for a short while. When I got back to New York, everybody wanted me to stay there, so I decided I would just stay there. I would just stay in New York. That's where Jimmy Ryan come in, see. Now we, now we're on the right road.
